To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

soil seed banks are poor indicators of mature vegetation composition, that they boost species richness and abundance both in early postfire and later seral fynbos stages and that they have a high persistence in alien plant invaded fynbos shrulands.

the seed bank is a good predictor of early post-fire fynbos species diversity but not of later seral stages, that the seed bank has a high potential to maintain species diversity in fynbos invaded by Acacia salignaa, and that the seed bank of the uninvading fynbos is a good predictor for the recovery of fynbos vegetation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of soil seed banks in fynbos shrulands, and the effects of alien plant invasion on the composition, structure and function of these communities.
the effects of alien Acacia on soil seed banks and the potential for restoration of fynbos vegetation.
the impacts of alien plant invasion on soil seed bank dynamics and the implications for restoration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
soil seed banks are important for the long-term persistence and recovery of invaded fynbos, and are a valuable resource in the conservation of fynbos biodiversity and ecosystem functioning.
the seed bank is a poor predictor of the mature vegetation composition and guild structure in fynboss.
soil seed banks in fynbos have high potential to contribute to the regeneration of the vegetation, especially if the alien Acacia is removed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the seed bank is an important reservoir of species richness, diversity, and long-lived seeders in uninvaded and long-invaded fyncbos and is therefore an important component of fynbos resilience.

soil-stored seed bank communities are a good predictor of the species composition of the early seral vegetation in fynbos and can provide an insight into the species that will dominate the mature vegetation.
the seed banks of fynbos and invaded fynbos are very diverse and species-rich.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the seed bank is a valuable resource that can buffer against the impacts of invasion.

soil seed banks are an important reservoir for fynbos biodiversity, particularly in the early stages after fire and in the later seral stages when many of the serotinous species have been lost from the vegetation.

seed banks in un-invaded fynbo are good indicators of species diversity and abundance in the mature fynbos, however, they may be poor indicators of the vegetation in invaded sites, especially if the invasion is recent.
